anti_generic_signature_read: An observatory dome whose shutter is open and whose telescope is out, lifting off a board that is already set up, with the pieces marked as the two bodies the telescope is pointed at.
blind_action_read: The domed lid lifts off the tray to expose a playing surface with 24 counters laid out staggered, twelve cream and twelve terracotta, in a draughts opening setup; closed, the counters are stored in the layer beneath the lid plate and visible through the rim gap.
blind_form_read: A wide smooth spherical-cap dome on a drum with a continuous seam round its base, on a square backing plate; one straight parallel-sided slot cut through dome and drum on one meridian, over the apex; a cylindrical barrel lying in the slot with its muzzle projecting, held by a fork of brackets rising from the slot floor.
blind_held_read: A domed observatory building on a plinth, shutter open, telescope in the opening, sitting as a lid on a shallow tray full of counters.
blind_relationship_read: Architectural cover directly above its own square board and the two opposing complete starting arrays; container and contents. The mark on the counters and the object on the lid belong to the same subject: sun and moon below, the dome that watches them above.
blind_subjects_read: Two sides of round discs, perfect circles: terracotta ones carrying an eight-ray sunburst around a round central pocket, read as the sun; cream ones carrying a crescent groove with a horn at each end, read as a crescent moon. Each disc carries the same mark on both faces, one face adding a crown groove that leaves the mark on a raised plateau.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4, unprompted, on all three lid frames: 'A domed observatory building on a plinth, shutter open, telescope in the opening'; 'An observatory dome with the shutter open and a telescope inside'; 'An observatory dome seen head-on, shutter open, telescope in the slit.' In round 1 the same critic read the lid as a computer mouse and never said observatory.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Roof reads as an observatory or telescope dome to an unprimed reader

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 2: 'a straight-walled cut of near-constant width', 'its two edges run close to parallel'. Round 4: 'the slot runs the full height', and every lid frame reads it as an open shutter.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: One shutter slit, 30 mm wide, square-cut parallel walls, on a single meridian, running over the apex

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4 describes a wide smooth dome on a drum with a 'continuous undercut groove round the base' - the seam - and reports no surface detail on the cap itself beyond tessellation banding.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A drum 180 mm across rising 14 mm, one rotation-ring seam round it, and a smooth spherical-cap dome on top

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'A cylindrical tube - a telescope barrel - sitting in the open slot... Solid object with a definite shape, not a lump', and 'Yes, it is held... together reading as a fork or yoke mount.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A telescope: blunt-ended 24 mm tube at 45 degrees emerging through the slit, carried on a fork of two arms rising from a solid pier

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'Nothing is visibly detached or floating. I looked specifically for islands; every bracket element appears to touch either the tube or the slot wall.' Measured: check_overhang at 45 degrees reports 0 unsupported regions on base and roof, and one bridged region per counter at 9.6 mm and 4.8 mm span, inside the 12 mm allowance.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: nothing about the telescope is floating, cantilevered, detached or unsupported, and no surface overhangs more than 45 degrees

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: No reader in any round described a cone, chimney, railing, ladder, rib, rivet, window or ornament. Across four rounds the only features named on the lid were the dome, the seam, the slot, the tube and its mount, on a plain 'square base plate'.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: the truncated cone, the telescope hood and the hood buttress are gone, nothing else is added to the roof (no railing, walkway, ladder, panelling, ribs, rivets, windows or decoration), the dome stays smooth and the backing plate has no notches, cut-outs or holes

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'Both discs are perfect circles. I checked the whole circumference of each: no tail, tab, notch, slot, spur or flat.' Confirmed independently on the near-plan and three-quarter frames.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Counters are plain round discs with a perfect circular outline, and NEGATIVE: no tail, tab, notch, slot or projection anywhere

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'Cream disc (7 vs 8): the sunk mark is now the SAME on both faces... Orange disc (5 vs 6): the sunk mark is the SAME on both faces.' In round 3 the same critic found the moon king face blank; that was repaired and re-read.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The same symbol is sunk into BOTH faces of a counter, so its owner reads whichever way up it lies

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'the identical eight-ray sunburst with its round central pocket'; it was read as the sun unprompted in every round, and no reader called it a gear, cog or sprocket. Geometry: rays span r3.2 to r4.97 with a 1.0 mm undisturbed band at the ball and 0.6 mm raised gaps between neighbours.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Sun counter: a round ball dead centre with eight separate little rays round it, and NEGATIVE: the rays touch neither the ball nor each other, so the mark is not a gear, cog or sprocket

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Manager inspection of the component packet: 'eight separate wedge pockets round it, each visibly wider at the inner end and narrowing to a blunt flat tip.' Geometry: 2.0 mm at the inner end, 1.0 mm flat tip. No reader described the rays as widening outwards.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: every sun ray is widest at its inner end and narrows outwards to a blunt flat tip

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'It is a crescent - a slim, sharply tapered sunk groove with a horn at each end... it depicts a crescent moon.' No reader described a point, spike or sliver in any round. Geometry: each horn ends in a flat square face 2.17 mm across.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Moon counter: one bold crescent with both horns truncated square, and NEGATIVE: no horn tapers to a point or to a thin sliver

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'one face adds the crown groove, leaving the crescent on a raised plateau', and the opposite face of each disc is described as a plain flat face carrying the mark and nothing else.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The king face carries a flat annular rebate round the edge leaving a raised plateau; the man face is flat and plain

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4: 'Yes, there is a clear unbroken flat band between the crescent and the edge of the plateau. I traced it right round - above the upper horn, outboard of the right tip, below and left of the tail - uninterrupted flat plateau at every point.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: MARGIN: a clear, unbroken, flat band of undisturbed material separates the symbol from what surrounds it on both faces

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4 on the playing frame: 'Yes, reliably, by two independent cues... every orange counter shows the dark speckled rosette, every cream counter shows a small distinct dark curl. Neither mark is absent. Strip the colour out and you could still separate the groups.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A Sun is distinguishable from a Moon across a populated board at distance

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round 4 on the closed frame: 'Yes. The domed lid sits on a shallow grey tray and the tray is full of counters... a continuous row of orange discs - eight visible, lying flat.' And: 'no crowned/ringed piece appears anywhere on the board - all 24 show plain faces.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The complete starting position still stores inside the closed roof, and the counters start man face up

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Not visual properties. cad/part_base.step reproduces the published hash 590aa6c78a8480f8d07e9344af11f075f2dc4350cd8a27462bc8ae4453e8f72c exactly and measure/check_fit.py asserts it every run; groups/observatory.json still carries base, roof, single_01..12 and forked_01..12; the roof measures 182.4 mm square and reaches z77.07 closed, inside the published roof's z77.23. Blind support: every round described the same tray, board and corner posts unchanged.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE: the base does not change, no part key changes, and nothing protrudes that did not protrude before

largest_risk: Direction dependence of the dome's outline. Viewed square-on to the slit meridian (snap/roof/az0_el12.png, snap/closed/az0_el8.png, both kept in the evidence) the shutter is edge-on and invisible, and in rounds 2 and 3 this same blind critic read that view as a computer mouse. Every view that can see into the slot reads as an observatory immediately. The specified envelope forces this: a 180 mm cap only 40 mm high with a meridian slit cannot show its opening from a direction perpendicular to it, and a 24 mm tube at 45 degrees inside z78 can only project about 20 mm. Second risk: the marks are 1.2 mm recesses, and this flat-lit renderer shades only their walls, never their floors, so the near-plan counter frames understate them - at 82 degrees the crowned moon reads as a line over an arc. A printed part reads a 1.2 mm recess by shadow; nothing here proves that.
resolution: Four rounds, one critic, blind throughout. Round 1 failed requirement A outright: the lid read as a computer mouse and the reader never said observatory. Round 2, after the shutter slit was stopped short of the far rim so the cap stays unbroken, the three-quarter frame read as 'an astronomical observatory dome with its shutter open and a telescope poking out'. Round 3 added fork prongs clear above the tube and cut the crescent back so it clears the king plateau by 2.0 mm instead of 1.0 mm; it also found the moon king face still blank. Round 4 confirmed the cause was presentation - flipping a disc mirrors its mark away from this renderer's lighting - and, with the king faces turned to the same bearing, found the same mark on both faces of both counters with an unbroken band round it, both sides distinguishable across the board, the starting position stored inside, nothing floating, and every lid frame reading as an observatory dome on first sight. No blocking defect survives. Two findings the critic called blocking are recorded instead as disclosed limitations, because both are properties the correction brief requires to stay as published: the roof has no grip or latch because no skirt, hinge, latch or hardware may be added, and the near-plan legibility of a 1.2 mm recess is a limit of the renderer, not of the geometry.
reviewer: one independent native critic, blind to the Wish, the brief and the product identity for all four rounds; never told what the object was
